prompt.context_jp: 甘春総合病院の一日___、慌ただしい定時診療のリズムの中で始まる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春総合病院の一日___、慌ただしい定時診療のリズムの中で始まる。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks 'a day at the hospital' as the established topic of this opening narration.

feedback.correct_en: This is the opening narrative frame introducing 'a day at the hospital' as the topic the sentence will describe. は sets up the theme.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new, identifying information in a reporting style, which doesn't fit this generalizing narration. を would require a transitive verb.

contrast_examples.en: A day at the hospital is busy. (topic)

contrast_examples.jp: 病院の一日が始まった。
contrast_examples.en: A day at the hospital began. (new event)

prompt.context_jp: その慌ただしさの陰で、画像を読み解く放射線科医の存在___、しばしば忘れられがちだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: ...放射線科医の存在___、しばしば忘れられがちだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'the radiologists' existence' as the topic being commented on.

feedback.correct_en: は presents 'the radiologist's existence' as the topic the narrator wants to comment on — namely that it is often forgotten. This is thematic framing.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like a new-information report ('a radiologist exists!'), which doesn't fit the reflective tone.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼の存在は忘れられがちだ。
contrast_examples.en: His presence tends to be forgotten. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 客席___まばらで、期待していたほどの人数は集まっていない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 客席___まばらで、期待していたほどの人数は集まっていない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the audience as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 客席 — the narrator describes the state of the audience as sparse. Combined with the following 人数は, parallel topic framing is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would give a 'the audience is sparse!' discovery reading, but this is calm reflective description, not news.

contrast_examples.en: The audience is sparse. (describing a known subject)

prompt.context_jp: 会場の隅には、五十嵐唯織の姿___あった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 会場の隅には、五十嵐唯織の姿___あった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces Igarashi's figure as newly noticed in the scene.

feedback.correct_en: This is classic existential/new-information が — the camera 'discovers' Igarashi in the corner. The pattern ...には〜があった uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply Igarashi is already the topic being discussed, but he is just being introduced into the scene.

contrast_examples.en: There was a cat in the corner. (new info)
That cat was in the corner. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 彼の胸に何か___小さくざわめいた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼の胸に何か___小さくざわめいた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'something stirred in his chest.'

feedback.correct_en: 何か ('something') is indefinite new information — the subject of a spontaneous emotional event. が is required with 何か here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 何かは would imply contrast ('as for something...'), which is nonsensical for an indefinite. を needs a transitive verb.

prompt.context_jp: 放射線科医___ 普段 直接 患者を治せるわけじゃないからね
prompt.prompt_jp: 放射線科医___ 普段 直接 患者を治せるわけじゃないからね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'radiologists' as the topic in Tsujimura's general statement about them.

feedback.correct_en: Tsujimura is making a generic statement about radiologists as a category — classic topical は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would single out radiologists as 'the ones who,' sounding like contrastive identification rather than a general explanation.

prompt.context_jp: 右胸に腫瘤___ありますね
prompt.prompt_jp: 右胸に腫瘤___ありますね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'a mass is present on the right breast.'

feedback.correct_en: This is new-information が — An is pointing out a finding (a mass) that she just identified in the image. Existence verb ある takes が for the item that exists.
feedback.incorrect_en: 腫瘤は would presuppose the mass is already known/under discussion. Here she is announcing its presence for the first time.

contrast_examples.en: There's a shadow here. (pointing it out)

prompt.context_jp: 患者さん___ 本当のことを知りたいと思います
prompt.prompt_jp: 患者さん___ 本当のことを知りたいと思います
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle framing 'patients' as the general topic in Igarashi's claim.

feedback.correct_en: Igarashi is making a generic statement about patients as a category and what they want. Generic subject → は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrow the reading to a specific identified patient wanting the truth, losing the general argument.

prompt.context_jp: とっくに 勤務時間 過ぎてるけど
prompt.prompt_jp: 勤務時間___ とっくに過ぎてるけど
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks '(your) working hours' as a contrastive topic ('working hours, at least...').

feedback.correct_en: は topicalizes 勤務時間 and carries an implicit contrast — 'as for working hours (contrary to your continued presence), they're long over.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report the fact neutrally and lose the pointed 'you're still here even though...' nuance Tamaki conveys.

contrast_examples.en: The time, at least, is already past. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 背後から声をかけたの___、いつのまにか出勤していた小野寺技師長だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 背後から声をかけたの___、...小野寺技師長だった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in the 'the one who X was Y' identification sentence.

feedback.correct_en: This is a 'the one who did X was Y' cleft: 〜のは〜だった. The nominalized clause is the topic, and 小野寺 is the identifying predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が here would try to make it 'someone called out from behind,' breaking the cleft structure that reveals the identity.

contrast_examples.en: The one who called was my mother.

prompt.context_jp: 私___ 母を乳がんで亡くして
prompt.prompt_jp: 私___ 母を乳がんで亡くして
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle Kyoko uses to introduce herself as the topic of a personal story.

feedback.correct_en: Kyoko opens a self-narrative — 'As for me, I lost my mother...' Topical は is standard for first-person life stories.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would answer 'who?' — identifying her as the one who lost her mother, suitable only if that question was asked.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be the one to go. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 最後に 自分の命を守れるの___ 自分だけなんです
prompt.prompt_jp: 自分の命を守れるの___ 自分だけなんです
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in Igarashi's emphatic exhaustive statement.

feedback.correct_en: The pattern 〜のは〜だけ ('the one who X is only Y') is a cleft construction using は on the nominalized clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would attempt an exhaustive-listing reading but conflicts with のは cleft structure that frames 'the one who can protect your life' as topic.

contrast_examples.en: The only one who can is you.

prompt.context_jp: デンスブレストについて 教えてくれたの___ あなただけでした
prompt.prompt_jp: デンスブレストについて 教えてくれたの___ あなただけでした
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the cleft identifying 'you' as the only one who told her.

feedback.correct_en: Standard 〜のは〜だ cleft. は topicalizes 'the person who told me,' and あなただけ is the identifying predicate.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would try an identificational reading but breaks the のは cleft pattern that Kyoko uses to emphasize gratitude.

contrast_examples.jp: 助けてくれたのは彼だ。
contrast_examples.en: The one who helped me was him.

prompt.context_jp: 一番 不安なの___ ご本人です
prompt.prompt_jp: 一番 不安なの___ ご本人です
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle in Igarashi's 'the one most anxious is the patient' line.

feedback.correct_en: Cleft 〜のは〜だ: 'The one who is most anxious is the patient herself.' は topicalizes the nominalized clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: が doesn't fit the のは〜です cleft frame that lets Igarashi redirect attention from Hirose's nerves to the patient's.

prompt.context_jp: 威能圭___ぽつりと呟いた一言が、皆の耳をそっと引き寄せた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 威能圭___ぽつりと呟いた一言が、皆の耳をそっと引き寄せた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking Inou Kei as the subject inside the relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause ('a word that Kei muttered'), the subject takes が (or の). は cannot normally appear in a non-contrastive relative clause.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to make 威能圭 the main sentence topic, but he is the subject only of the embedded clause describing 一言.

prompt.context_jp: 患者を直接治すことはできなくとも、正しい診断へ___役割は決して小さくない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 正しい診断へ___役割
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with '正しい診断へ' meaning 'guide to.'

feedback.correct_en: 診断へ導く ('to guide/lead to a diagnosis') is the standard collocation for guiding someone to a conclusion or outcome.
feedback.incorrect_en: 運ぶ ('carry') and 渡す ('hand over') don't collocate with abstract goals like 診断.

prompt.context_jp: 参加者の少なさに___杏を、辻村は柔らかな声で慰めようとする。
prompt.prompt_jp: 参加者の少なさに___杏
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the expression meaning 'drops her shoulders in disappointment.'

feedback.correct_en: 肩を落とす is a set phrase for being dejected/disappointed — exactly An's state after the sparse turnout.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options are not idiomatic for disappointment and sound unnatural.

contrast_examples.en: He was disheartened by the result.
to be proud (lit. puff out chest)

prompt.context_jp: 鏡に映った自分の姿に、彼女は思わず___。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女は思わず息を___。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb forming the idiom 'to gasp / catch one's breath.'

feedback.correct_en: 息を呑む is the set idiom for being so surprised one momentarily holds one's breath — fits Hirose's shock at the mirror.
feedback.incorrect_en: 息を吸う is just 'inhale'; 息を止める is 'hold one's breath' intentionally (as during a scan). Neither captures the involuntary surprise.

prompt.context_jp: 右胸に腫瘤がありますね 辺縁が___で 悪性の可能性も否定できません
prompt.prompt_jp: 辺縁が___で 悪性の可能性も否定できません
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the adjective describing an irregular tumor margin suggesting malignancy.

feedback.correct_en: 辺縁不整 ('irregular margin') is standard radiology terminology for a worrying mass. Smooth margins would suggest benign.
feedback.incorrect_en: 滑らか would suggest benign features — the opposite diagnosis. 透明 doesn't fit tumor description.

prompt.context_jp: ねぎらいの言葉を ___なければ
prompt.prompt_jp: ねぎらいの言葉を ___なければ
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that collocates with 言葉を to mean 'offer words (to someone).'

feedback.correct_en: 言葉をかける is the standard phrase meaning to 'address someone' with words — exactly fits offering words of appreciation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言葉を言う is redundant and unnatural. 言葉をやる doesn't exist as a set phrase.

prompt.context_jp: 相変わらず 汚っ ___ 男ができないわけね
prompt.prompt_jp: ___ 男ができないわけね
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the connective meaning 'no wonder / that's why.'

feedback.correct_en: どうりで ('no wonder') introduces an explanation for an observation — Tamaki links the messy room to An's lack of a boyfriend.
feedback.incorrect_en: どうやら means 'apparently' and どうにか means 'somehow'; neither carries the causal 'that explains it' meaning.

prompt.context_jp: ___が悪いな すぐに 超音波検査した方が よさそうだ
prompt.prompt_jp: ___が悪いな
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun used idiomatically to describe a 'nasty-looking' tumor shadow.

feedback.correct_en: In radiology jargon 顔つきが悪い means a lesion 'looks suspicious/nasty' — the shadow has an ominous appearance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気分 and 機嫌 refer to a person's mood, not an image feature.

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi is a technician asking a patient he just stopped on the street to come back for more testing.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds more natural for a hospital technician addressing a stranger patient?

choices.text: 早めに 超音波検査を 受けてもらえませんか？
早く 超音波検査 受けてよ。

feedback.correct_en: 〜てもらえませんか is polite-request form appropriate for a medical professional asking a stranger a favor.
feedback.incorrect_en: 受けてよ is a casual command tone that would be rude from a technician to a patient he's never met.

contrast_examples.jp: 手伝ってもらえませんか。

prompt.context_jp: Kyoko confronting the hospital about not being told about dense breasts.
prompt.prompt_en: Which emotional phrasing is more natural for Kyoko's frustration?

choices.text: 私たち 知りようがないじゃないですか
私たち 知る方法がないじゃないですか

feedback.correct_en: 〜ようがない ('there's no way to~') is the natural idiomatic form, carrying emotional helplessness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 知る方法がない is grammatically possible but sounds flat and bookish compared to the emotional, idiomatic 知りようがない.

prompt.context_jp: Kaburagi explaining departmental policy to An in a formal workplace tone.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sentence sounds more natural as a senior radiologist's measured policy statement?

choices.text: 我々は "異常なし"と 書くほかありませんよ
我々は "異常なし"って 書くしかないよ

feedback.correct_en: 〜ほかありません is a formal written/spoken register fitting Kaburagi's authoritative, policy-citing stance.
feedback.incorrect_en: 〜しかない with って and よ is casual coworker register — too informal for the measured institutional tone shown here.

contrast_examples.en: We have no choice but to comply. (formal)
Gotta just go along with it. (casual)

prompt.context_jp: Igarashi pleading on Kyoko's behalf, invoking her late mother.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing is more natural for 'a life that might have been saved'?

choices.text: 早期に発見ができれば 助かった命かもしれません
早期に発見ができれば 助かる命だったかもしれません

feedback.correct_en: 助かった命 (past form directly modifying 命) is a tight, emotionally charged phrase meaning 'a life that could have been saved.' It is the idiomatic choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: 助かる命だった is grammatically fine but longer and less punchy — it dilutes the counterfactual regret.

contrast_examples.en: a life that could have been saved
